plan: Can I stop for groceries on the way?
text: My professor moved Thursday's lab to finish at 4:15. I need to pick up my sister when her practice ends at 5. The drive normally takes 25 to 45 minutes. Can I stop for groceries on the way?
My flight lands at 6:20, but my dinner reservation is at 7:30. It usually takes half an hour to get out of the airport and another 20 to 50 minutes to reach the restaurant.
I've got $450 left for discretionary spending this month. I already committed $180 to a birthday present. I'm considering buying headphones for $210 and concert tickets for $125.
I need to leave work by 4 to make my dentist appointment. My manager just scheduled a meeting that ends at 4:30. That meeting cannot be moved.
My friend wants dinner around seven, but she hasn't confirmed the reservation.

plan: Which interview time should I trust?
text: My calendar says the interview is at 2, but the recruiter's newer email says 3. I'm not sure whether the calendar invitation was updated.

plan: Can I drive to the airport?
text: My partner needs the car from 3 until 6. I was planning to drive to the airport at 4.

plan: Can I get to the wedding?
text: I have to get to a wedding by 5, and my train arrives at 4:15.
If it rains, the ceremony moves indoors and starts half an hour earlier.
My class ends at 3:30. The drive to the station takes 15-35 minutes, the train leaves at 4:10, and parking takes another 5-12 minutes.
